title: Email overload: exploring personal information management of email
abstract: Field observations showed that email had expanded beyond communication into task management and personal archiving. Users kept messages representing outstanding tasks, partially processed documents, and ongoing conversations in their inboxes, creating overload and making important work difficult to track.

title: What a to-do: studies of task management towards the design of a personal task list manager
abstract: The authors studied the media people use to record and organize to-dos and followed how tasks are completed over time. They found that users employ sophisticated prioritization strategies and identified factors influencing task completion and the usefulness of different task representations.

title: eAssistant: Cognitive Assistance for Identification and Auto-Triage of Actionable Conversations
abstract: eAssistant identifies actionable information such as requests and promises across productivity applications including email, chat, messaging, and enterprise collaboration tools. Its action-identification model is personalizable, online-trainable, and continuously updated from user interactions and feedback, and it uses user-centric conversation characteristics for auto-triage.

title: Uncertainty Visualizations: Helping Decision Makers Become More Aware of Uncertainty and Its Implications
abstract: The authors develop and evaluate a domain-independent decision-support system that visualizes uncertainty when available information is insufficient to distinguish alternatives. The interface highlights ambiguity and identifies additional information that could reduce it, directly linking uncertainty presentation to information seeking and decision support.
venue: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making
